description_preview:
We are Skyward.
That is, a love for people, for improvement, for human advancement through information technology. We are a people-centered business with a desire to serve others. We are diverse and unified; creative and collaborative; a collection of complementary, not competing talents. And though on the surface we remain relaxed, beneath, a torrent of energy links us to our civic tech mission.
We stand by our values, and we won’t compromise on any of them.
Integrity:
We’re conscientious, intentional, and empathetic. Our words and actions align. That’s our character. Please don’t ask us to play another part, we’re poor actors.
Compassionate:
If we may borrow a quote from Theodore Roosevelt: “No one cares how much you know until they know how much you care.” Because our team is thoughtful and supportive, caring deeply for each other, our clients, and our work, this comes naturally.
Inquisitive:
We remain students by failing openly and turning lessons into solutions.
Unconventional:
For us, life isn’t what happens outside of work. Work happens inside of life and our culture erases the line often dividing the two.
Authentic:
Made possible only because we embody the values listed above. We’re relaxed and fun yet intensely curious and driven. Team members are placed with thought, care, and precision to ensure that Trust, Truth, and Transparency continue to represent our brand.
Because of that, we continue Onward, Upward, and Skyward.
We Need a Software Engineer Who Does It All.
Would your friends say you can dissect a complex problem until it quietly gives up? Have you been told (more than once) that you care suspiciously much about modernizing the crusty old systems powering public services ? Good. We’re not bored, we’re impressed.
Here’s the thing: we don’t want an engineer who only writes code and tosses it over the wall. We want the rare one who writes it, automates the pipeline that ships it, and builds the tests that prove it works, and then sleeps soundly because of it. If you believe “done” means tested, deployed, and monitored (not “it runs on my laptop”), then we want you.
Come join us if you're motivated to learn from others, to learn from mistakes, to be part of a future-looking and growth-oriented team.
Let's go Skyward together.
What you’ll do:
Build things that matter. Write effective, scalable code supporting CMS as it merges systems into one AI-driven platform - reducing manual effort, improving data accuracy, and bringing cutting-edge NLP and LLM techniques to public services
Automate all the toil. Own CI/CD pipelines end to end, automating build, test, and deployment workflows with tools like Jenkins, plus Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible) so deployments are boring in the best possible way
Test like you mean it. Build and maintain automated test suites - unit, integration, regression - wired straight into the pipeline as quality gates, and provide real test-coverage analysis instead of crossed fingers
Containerize and ship. Package and deploy workloads with Docker (and friends) for repeatable, scalable, what-you-build-is-what-you-run environments
Hunt the bugs. Investigate and debug test failures throughout the lifecycle, update tests or file bugs as needed, and keep the build green and honest
Bake in security. Integrate code-quality checks and security gates (think SonarQube, Snyk) into the pipeline so problems get caught before they ship, not after
Design with humans in mind. Work closely with human-centered design experts to build solutions that are intuitive, responsive, and personalized to each user’s needs
Make things faster. Develop and tune back-end components to improve responsiveness and overall performance
What we’d like you to have:
3-5 years of hands-on software engineering experience, with strong coding chops in Python (and friends)
Real DevOps / DevSecOps / DevTestOps experience. You know CI/CD isn’t a buzzword; you’ve actually automated build, test, and deployment workflows
Test automation skill. You’ve built automated tests and integrated them into pipelines with code-quality checks and security gates, not bolted them on at the end
A feel for good pipelines. Scalable, maintainable, and integrated with testing frameworks. You know, the kind that make the whole team faster
Containerization experience (Docker or Kubernetes) and comfort with REST APIs
Fluency in an agile flavor or two - Scrum, Lean, or SAFe
Strong communication and interpersonal skills to work effectively across a busy mix of stakeholders
What would blow us away:
You’ve got AI chops, experience with NLP, LLMs, or ML-driven applications
You’ve previously supported CMS or another federal agency
Bonus unicorn points if you’ve worked inside a FISMA boundary or supported an ATO/cATO effort
Even if you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications, we encourage you to apply. At Skyward, we’re focused on hiring individuals with the right skills and passion to grow, not just checking off every box.
And now the important part. What we offer you:
Medical, dental, vision insurance
15 days of paid leave
7 days of sick leave
2 days bereavement leave
11 paid Federal holidays
Up to 40 hours for jury duty
401K with 4% employer contribution (and no vesting period)
Up to 4 weeks of paid paternity and maternity leave
Company provided laptop
$5,000 per year for professional development
$600 per year for technical supplies and equipment
$2,000 referral bonus
Life and disability insurance
HSA and FSA
Legal Shield and ID Shield Voluntary Benefits

About Charta Health
In an industry where the focus should rightly be on delivering quality care to patients, healthcare providers remain burdened by the complexities of non-clinical operations. Charta is changing that.
We're building the operating system for modern healthcare organizations. Our AI platform streamlines critical workflows across revenue cycle, clinical operations, and administrative functions, helping providers and payers operate more efficiently and deliver better patient care. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Charta is on a mission to make every healthcare dollar accountable and every chart accurate, reimagining healthcare infrastructure from the ground up.
About The Opportunity
We're looking for a Support Engineer to be the first technical line of defense behind our customer-facing team. When a client reports that something looks wrong - a chart that wasn't processed, a code that didn't appear, an integration that stopped sending data, an output that doesn't match what the clinician documented - you are the person who figures out what actually happened, why, and what it would take to fix it.
This is not a customer-facing role. Our Technical Success Managers own the client relationship and deliver outcomes to customers. You own the investigation behind them: reproducing the issue, tracing it to a root cause in data, logs, configuration, or code, resolving what you can directly, and handing Engineering a well-scoped diagnosis and proposed fix for what you can't. Your work is what lets our customer team give clients fast, accurate answers - and what protects our engineers' time for building.
Every account is mapped to an owning engineering pod, so you will always know where an escalation goes. You are accountable for the quality of the triage decision and for making sure nothing reaches an engineer that you could have resolved or scoped yourself.
What You'll Do
Investigate and Diagnose: Take incoming issues from the Technical Success team - bugs, data discrepancies, processing gaps, unexpected model output - and dig in hands-on. Reproduce the problem, query the data, read logs and pipeline runs, and trace the issue to a root cause.
Triage with Judgment: Classify every issue quickly and correctly: live incident vs. one-off, deployment/configuration issue vs. product bug vs. expected behavior vs. feature gap. Route incidents to oncall, bugs and gaps to the owning pod, and close out anything that is working as designed - with the evidence to show it.
Resolve What You Can (Tier 1): Fix configuration, mapping, and data issues directly; re-run failed jobs; correct customer-specific setup; and answer "did Charta do this?" questions with a definitive, evidence-backed yes or no.
Propose Fixes (Tier 2): For code-level defects, go beyond "it's broken." Identify where in the codebase the problem lives, write up the root cause, and propose a fix - up to and including drafting the change for engineering review. Engineers should receive a ticket they can act on, not a mystery.
Hand Off Cleanly to the Customer Team: Give the Technical Success Manager a clear, plain-English summary of what happened, what was affected, what's being done, and a realistic timeline - so they can deliver the message to the client with confidence.
Own the Loop Internally: Track every open issue from intake to resolution. Follow up with Engineering, confirm fixes in production, and tell the customer team when it's safe to close the loop with the client.
Build the Knowledge Base: Turn every investigation into reusable knowledge - runbooks, known-issue write-ups, diagnostic queries, and triage guides - so the same question takes minutes, not hours, the next time, and so the customer team can self-serve more over time.
Spot Patterns: Aggregate issues across accounts to surface recurring defects, fragile integrations, and gaps in monitoring or tooling. Bring data-driven recommendations to Product and Engineering about what to fix at the source.
You'd Be a Great Fit, If You
Are Technically Strong. You are comfortable reading code (Python and/or TypeScript), writing SQL, working through logs and data pipelines, and using AI coding tools to move quickly through an unfamiliar codebase. You can work alongside engineers as a peer.
Are a Relentless Debugger. When something doesn't add up, your instinct is to dig until you find the real cause - not the first plausible one. You rule out the obvious (Is there a live incident? Was there a recent deploy? Is this reproducible?) before you escalate.
Figure It Out Yourself. This role runs on documentation, tooling, and your own initiative. You are self-sufficient in the weeds and come back with answers, not questions.
Write Excellent Tickets. Your escalations are clear, reproducible, and scoped: what happened, the evidence, the suspected cause, the blast radius, and a proposed fix. Engineers are glad to receive them.
Translate Technical to Plain English. You can explain a root cause to an engineer in one message and to a non-technical teammate in the next.

Handle Sensitive Data Responsibly. You understand that healthcare data demands care, and you follow access and privacy practices without shortcuts.

title: Software Development Engineer II, Data Center Software (DC BRIDGE)
reason: Stack +43; Title fit +6; Entry +15; US +10
description_preview:
Description
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
DC BRIDGE builds the software that makes AWS data centers, and the people who operate them, more efficient, so AWS stays ahead of its physical growth. Every data center depends on electrical, mechanical, and controls equipment staying within limits. We build the services that monitor that equipment at fleet scale (trillions of metrics a month), turn the alarm firehose into signal operators can act on, route work to the engineers who run the buildings, and keep the devices in those buildings on the right software. What we ship affects the availability and efficiency of the infrastructure behind AWS.
This is a builder role on a team that ships. Small groups of SDEs own their services end-to-end and deploy to production several times a week. As an SDE II you own features from design through operation. Your customers, the engineers who run the buildings, are a message away. Our generative AI strategy is still forming; your prototypes shape it.
Tech stack: Java, Python, and TypeScript, with Kotlin, Go, and Rust in specific services. AWS CDK and CloudFormation. Lambda, ECS, Fargate, DynamoDB, SQS, SNS, S3, Kinesis, Step Functions, API Gateway, CloudWatch, Athena, Amazon Bedrock. Amazon's internal CI/CD. AI-assisted development tools daily.
Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate distributed services for data center infrastructure: metric ingestion and stream processing at fleet scale; alarm evaluation, suppression, correlation, and deduplication; automated triage and routing; telemetry persistence and analytics; and the services and on-device agents that manage industrial control devices.
Build the integrations that route alarms and tickets to operations teams with the context they need to resolve them faster.
Apply generative AI where it earns its place: integrate services such as Amazon Bedrock for summarization, pattern detection, and triage assistance, and use AI-assisted development tools to prototype, test, and review faster. Integrate and measure, not train models.
Drive efficiency at scale: simplify systems, deprecate what the fleet no longer needs, and cut the cost per metric and per device as the fleet grows.
Define infrastructure as code with AWS CDK, wire up CI/CD, and own what you deploy.
Author designs with trade-off analysis and give meaningful feedback in design reviews.
Join on-call, find root causes, write permanent fixes, and drive the practices that keep quality high.
Mentor earlier-career engineers through code review and pairing, including effective use of AI tools while keeping code ownership and understanding.
A day in the life
Your morning might start with standup, sharing progress on a new alarm evaluation or device management feature, then a code review where you give thoughtful feedback to an SDE I. You spend a focused block writing service or stream-processing code, or CDK to wire up a new pipeline, then debug a production issue that surfaced overnight, finding the root cause and writing a permanent fix. After lunch you join a design review, asking the questions that surface unstated assumptions. You wrap up walking through alarm or tooling feedback with a data center operations or controls team, turning what you hear into the next improvement.
About The Team
DC BRIDGE teams operate with high ownership and autonomy over their services end-to-end, from design through production operation. Each team is a small group of SDEs who run everything they build. Our mission is to give the people who run Amazon's data centers a clear, trustworthy picture of the fleet and the tools to act on it: every alarm should mean something, every metric should be worth what it costs to process, and every device should be running the software it should. As an SDE II you'll be a core autonomous contributor: owning features, raising the bar in reviews, and helping more junior engineers grow.
*Why AWS*
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
*Diverse Experiences*
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
*Work/Life Balance*
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
*Inclusive Team Culture*
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud

Description
Customer experience is at the heart of all we do at Amazon, as we strive to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Amazon Customer Service (CS) is at the forefront of customer experience, working relentlessly to provide customers with a convenient, high quality, and delightful experience - across all our CS channels, in every interaction.
Within CS, Human in the Loop (HITL) engineering brings human judgment into AI-handled conversations in real time, across every use case, channel, and marketplace where automation reaches its limit. We build the systems that predict when a bot is about to fail. We summarize live conversation context so a Customer Service Associate can decide in seconds, and we execute that decision back into the conversation while the customer is still in it, with no transfer and nothing to re-explain. Every intervention also becomes training data for the next contact like it, so the case that needed a human this time is one automation can handle on its own the next. That is why HITL compounds instead of plateauing.
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build that platform and shape the architecture behind it. Today HITL runs tens of thousands of customer contacts every week across four use cases in the US, UK, and Canada. What stands between us and ten times that is the architecture itself. Core logic is spread across several services, each new use case takes about six weeks to launch, and tight coupling to our current bot stack blocks entire product lines where human judgment would matter most. You will be a significant contributor to fixing that. You will help design and build HITL as a standalone platform, shape the contracts that let any bot in CS request human judgment, and make the real-time path fast and reliable enough that a customer sitting in a live conversation never knows a human was involved.
Role
This is a high-ambiguity, high-ownership role. You will own components end to end, from the design doc through launch, and you will help make the calls on latency budgets, failure modes, and what the platform guarantees to the teams building on it. The problems are hard ones:
Orchestration across multiple customer service systems with no single owner
LLM inference inside a conversation a customer is waiting in
Triggering logic that has to be right at the moment it fires, not just in aggregate
A keep-alive mechanism that will not survive our next scale-up
Feedback pipelines that turn every associate decision into training data worth learning from.
You will work with applied scientists to move models from notebook to production path. You will partner with the teams who own the systems HITL depends on, and you will contribute to the engineering standards of the team through code and design review and by mentoring the engineers around you.
The person we are looking for likes problems where the right design is not obvious yet, cares about operational excellence because customers feel every regression, and wants to build AI systems that get measurably better every week because of the decisions they made.

Own the design and delivery of major HITL components, from technical design through production launch and ongoing operation.

title: Infrastructure Engineer
reason: Stack +56; Title fit +12; US +10; Overqualified -45
description_preview:
About Arena Intelligence
Arena is the platform for evaluating how AI models perform in the real world. Founded by researchers from UC Berkeley's SkyLab, we're on a mission to measure and advance the frontier of AI for real-world use, and to build the foundation for everyone to understand, shape, and benefit from it.
Tens of millions of people use Arena each month to evaluate how frontier systems handle the work they actually do. The preferences they share power the most transparent, rigorous, and human-centered evaluations in AI. Leading AI labs, enterprises, and independent researchers rely on our work and open datasets to understand how models behave in real workflows: agentic coding, creative generation, professional productivity, and beyond. We go beyond leaderboards and decompose what human experience reveals about AI, so models advance toward the work people actually do.
We're a team of researchers, academics, builders, and creatives from UC Berkeley, Google, Stanford, and DeepMind. We seek truth, move fast, and value craftsmanship, curiosity, and impact over hierarchy. We're building a company where thoughtful, curious people from all backgrounds can do their best work together, in an office culture that radiates excellence, energy, and focus.
About The Role
Arena Intelligence is looking for an Infrastructure Engineer to build the core infrastructure that sits beneath our online evaluation systems — the AI gateways, automated arena runtimes, and serving layers that make real-world model evaluation possible at scale.
This is a critical part of the Arena Service. Arenas are live, online systems: they route traffic across frontier models from many providers, handle bursty and unpredictable load, need to fail gracefully when upstream models do, and have to remain fair and consistent under all of it. We exist to build foundational infrastructure for our users that scales, is reliable, and makes the complexities of operating this infrastructure at scale disappear. We need a practitioner who's shipped this kind of infrastructure before and knows where the sharp edges are.
You'll be an early member of our infrastructure team, working closely with researchers, engineers, and product leadership. The work is zero-to-one in places and scale-it-up in others. We move fast and stay rigorous.
What You'll Do
Build API-based products from the ground up. Design and implement low-latency, high-reliability APIs for leaderboards, models, and arenas.
Solve hard streaming problems. Handle SSE/streaming responses across heterogeneous providers, including partial failure recovery, mid-stream fallback, and consistent response normalization.
Ship enterprise-grade infrastructure. Build the systems enterprise customers expect: rate limiting, authentication, usage metering, cost attribution, audit logging, and SOC 2 compliance.
Build deep observability. Instrument infrastructure with distributed tracing, latency breakdowns, token-level usage tracking, and real-time dashboards so customers (and we) can see exactly what's happening.
Build AI-centered products. Integrate with our core evaluation platform, Arena data, and customer-specific benchmarks. Collaborate with the research team to turn novel ideas into full-featured products.
Flex across the stack. Contribute to the backend of our Leaderboards and Evals platforms when needed, helping unify our public and private data architectures.
You’ll have
4+ years of backend engineering experience, with meaningful time spent on distributed systems, infrastructure, or developer-facing platforms.
Strong proficiency in Go and/or Rust, with hands-on experience building high-throughput APIs or proxy/gateway systems.
Experience with LLM provider APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) and a working understanding of the challenges: streaming, token management, rate limits, model-specific quirks.
Solid cloud infrastructure skills — you're comfortable with AWS or GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, and database systems like Postgres and Redis.
A product-oriented mindset. You think about the developer experience of your APIs, not just the implementation. You ask "why" before "how."
Comfort with ambiguity. We're a startup. Scope is fluid, context shifts, and you'll wear many hats. That should sound exciting, not stressful.
Nice to Have
Experience building API gateways, proxies, or developer tools (Bifrost, Kong, Envoy, Tyk, or custom).
Background in ML infrastructure, model serving, or evaluation frameworks.
Experience building enterprise-ready features: SSO, RBAC, audit logs, multi-tenancy.
Experience building billing infrastructure around systems like Stripe, Metronome and Orb
Familiarity with the modern AI infra stack (vLLM, LiteLLM, LangChain, etc.).
What we offer
We offer competitive compensation and equity aligned to the markets where our team members are based. The base salary range will depend on the candidate’s permanent work location.
Comprehensive health and wellness benefits, including medical, dental, vision, and additional support programs.
The opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI with a small, mission-driven team
A culture that values transparency, trust, and community impact
Come help build the space where anyone can explore and help shape the future of AI.

Job Description:

Life at Intel: https://jobs.intel.com/en/life-at-intel
As a Yield Development Engineer, you will be at the forefront of advancing Intel's cutting-edge process technologies within our Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization. This pivotal role involves identifying root cause yield limiters and driving solutions that enhance manufacturability and yield across technology nodes. You will work within a dynamic, fast-paced environment to ensure the successful introduction of new products, process improvements, and robust methodologies to meet manufacturing goals. Your expertise will directly contribute to Intel's ability to deliver world-class semiconductor solutions and advance the future of computing.
About Intel Foundry
At Intel, the Foundry Technology Development (TD) unit is the driving force behind Moore's Law, enabling us to create groundbreaking technology that enriches lives globally. With over 15,000 dedicated employees, Foundry TD spearheads innovative research, develops next-generation processes and packaging technologies, and manages high-volume manufacturing in state-of-the-art facilities. Within Intel Foundry TD, our Logic Technology Development (LTD) organization is at the forefront of creating and refining each process technology node, paving the way for tomorrow's computing solutions.
Your responsibilities as a Product Yield Development Engineer will include but not be limited to:
Develop methods, processes, and systems to consolidate and analyze diverse big data sources for defect mode understanding and yield modeling.
Perform statistical analysis, create visualizations, and construct process development roadmaps that drive technology yield milestones.
Extract insights from structured and unstructured data using advanced statistics, machine learning, and coding techniques.
Organize, interpret, and structure insights from fab process, defect, and electrical data while identifying anomalies to drive process changes for yield enhancement.
Develop multivariate algorithms and tools to identify root cause yield limiters and recommend process changes for yield improvement.
Collaborate with design teams to resolve yield issues, ensuring manufacturability across process and product specifications before ramping production.
Execute new product introductions, enable design-technology co-optimization, and participate in design of experiments with factory task forces.
Develop measurement recipes for rapid feedback on product integrity and address issues impacting yield or product quality.
Create and harden systems capable of meeting operational needs for leading-edge logic nodes, working with equipment vendors and internal collaborators.
Develop AI/ML applications and computational tools to bridge the gap between design and manufacturing, improve design efficiency, and reduce debug time.
Document technical procedures, train colleagues, and debug equipment, software, and procedural failures in production environments when required.

You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Project/program management experience with strong self-initiative and self-learning capabilities.

You start the morning reviewing feedback on a recently shipped feature and checking how it’s performing for collectors.

Later in the day, you’re in a product discussion about an upcoming drop, bringing both your web engineering perspective and your own TCG fluency to the conversation.

Job Description
A Software Engineer II is proficient with the most-often used features of the programming language, its core library, commonly used 3rd party libraries, and commonly used code management and build tooling.
Initially a Software Engineer II is expected to be able to develop a medium set of defined, inter-related modules, articulate why the code and application they are working on are designed the way they are, and be able to provide some instructive feedback to newer developers through code reviews and in-person Q&A. As they progress, they should be able to implement smaller subsystems independently, begin to design small portions of the systems, and begin to understand the design principles and practices that cut across all the applications.
The goals of a Software Engineer II are:
Develop an understanding of why some libraries, frameworks, and tooling are designed the way they are: what tradeoffs were made? why might the developer have done that? Through this work, develop an understanding of the practical use of design patterns.
Begin to understand some of the externalities associated with running an application: performance, security, operations, monitoring, etc.
Be able to troubleshoot application, infrastructure, and environment issues.
Or, more succinctly, the Software Engineer II is gaining the ability to determine why things are done in a particular way and apply that knowledge to new situations.

About ContractorHUB
ContractorHUB is building the AI-native operating system for home service businesses. We’re a small, fast-moving team building an ambitious product and rethinking how software gets developed along the way.
AI is already deeply integrated into how our team builds, tests, and ships software. We’re looking for an engineer who is excited about where that is headed and wants to help us lead the evolution of development in the industry. This role will define & own the standard for what “ready to ship” means at ContractorHUB.
The role
We’re looking for a Product Quality Engineer to own quality across the ContractorHUB platform.
This is an engineering role, not a traditional manual QA position. You’ll work directly in our Laravel/PHP codebase, investigate and fix issues, submit code, build automated testing, and help establish the systems and standards we use to confidently ship product.
You’ll also help us rethink QA for an AI-forward development environment. We want someone who is comfortable using AI throughout their own work and interested in finding better ways to automate testing, identify problems earlier, and improve the reliability of an increasingly fast development cycle.
What you'll do
Own product quality and help define what “done” looks like before features ship
Test new features across functionality, integrations, APIs, permissions, multi-tenant environments, browsers, and devices
Investigate bugs down to the code level, identify root causes, and submit fixes
Build and maintain automated tests that improve coverage and reduce regression risk
Use AI and automation to make testing faster, more thorough, and more scalable
Develop repeatable QA and release-readiness processes as our engineering organization grows
Work closely with Product and Engineering to identify risks earlier in the development process
Validate AI-powered product experiences, including behavior that isn't always deterministic
Help us move quickly without accepting “we'll fix it later” as the standard
You might be a fit if
You’re a software engineer who gets upset when something doesn't work the way it should
You have hands-on experience with PHP/Laravel or a background that will allow you to get productive in the stack quickly
You have experience with automated testing and understand when manual testing still matters
You can trace an issue from what a customer sees all the way back to what is happening in the code
You’re comfortable fixing problems yourself rather than simply documenting and handing them off
You’re excited about AI-assisted software development and already adopting these modern development approaches
You’re thorough without becoming a bottleneck
You can manage your own priorities and keep pushing until the work is actually finished
You want meaningful ownership without needing a management title
How we work
Our development process is highly AI-forward. We use AI throughout engineering, from writing and reviewing code to testing, troubleshooting, and accelerating development.
That lets a small team move incredibly quickly. It also raises the bar for how we think about quality—we don't mail it in. We need to ensure the highest standard of quality for our customers.
You’ll have the opportunity to help build that system with us: deciding where automation belongs, where human judgment matters, and how we create enough confidence in our product to keep increasing the speed at which we build.
You’ll report directly to Matt Parks, Founder & Chief Product & Innovation Officer, and work closely with the rest of our Product and Engineering team.
Compensation & logistics
Competitive compensation based on experience
Performance bonus opportunities
Health and dental benefits
Internet and phone stipend
Equity options
Remote-first team
To apply
We care about what you can do.
Tell us about something you’ve built, fixed, tested, or improved that demonstrates how you think as an engineer. We’re especially interested in examples where you found a problem others missed, built a better way to prevent it from happening again, or used AI and automation to improve how software gets shipped. Attach this info to your resume and send it our way.

Description
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?
At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to doing the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. Our Mission, Vision, and Values guide the way we do business.
Your greatest work is ahead!
Leidos Defense is seeking a talented
DevSecOps Engineer
to design, build, and secure the continuous integration, continuous delivery (CI/CD), and deployment infrastructure supporting advanced sensor and mission systems. This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy automating software pipelines, integrating automated security testing (SAST/DAST), and optimizing development infrastructure today, while growing into broader system-level deployment and real-time infrastructure architecture over time. We have offices across the United States engaging in the defense, space, cyber and commercial fields, we provide responsive, cost-effective engineering, scientific and IT solutions.
If this sounds like the kind of environment where you can thrive, keep reading!
Leidos Defense provides a diverse portfolio of systems, solutions, and services covering land, sea, air, space, and cyberspace for customers worldwide. Solutions for Defense include enterprise and mission IT, large-scale intelligence systems, command and control, geospatial and data analytics, cybersecurity, logistics, training, and intelligence analysis and operations support. Our team is solving the world’s toughest security challenges for customers with “can’t fail” missions.
Primary Responsibilities
Candidate will support advanced technology radar programs by automating, securing, and maintaining the infrastructure that compiles, tests, and deploys high-performance sensor and data processing applications. These systems are tightly coupled with real-time data pipelines and hardware, requiring a strong understanding of performant build systems, Linux optimization, and secure infrastructure.
Engineers in this role are expected to grow into broader pipeline and infrastructure ownership over time, contributing across application build management, automated security compliance, and deployment frameworks.
Design, implement, and maintain secure CI/CD pipelines to automate the build, test, and deployment environments for modern C++ applications.
Integrate and manage automated security tools (e.g., SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, and container vulnerability scanning) into the development lifecycle.
Automate infrastructure provisioning and configuration management using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles.
Collaborate closely with software, systems, and hardware engineers to optimize software compilation times, build scalability, and deployment reliability.
Support software integration and deployment in operational, simulated, and hardware-in-the-loop (HWIL) testing environments.
Enforce cybersecurity compliance and hardening guidelines (such as DISA STIGs) across Linux-based development and runtime environments.
Troubleshoot and resolve build failures, environment disparities, and pipeline bottlenecks to ensure high developer velocity.
Basic Qualifications
Candidate must possess a Bachelor's degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline from an ABET-accredited school with a strong demonstration of the skills listed below.
Candidate must have 2+ years of experience in DevSecOps, DevOps, or Software Engineering with a heavy focus on infrastructure and pipeline automation.
Candidate must have excellent teamwork skills and possess strong fundamentals in the following:
Strong experience building and managing CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar).
Proficiency in Linux-based environments, including advanced shell scripting, system administration, and performance tuning.
Experience with containerization technologies (e.g., Docker, Podman) and orchestration tools.
Strong experience with Python or other scripting languages for automation task development.
Familiarity with building and packaging compiled languages, specifically modern C++ applications.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative, cross-functional team environment.
US Citizenship is required and ability to obtain and maintain and DoD Secret clearance.
Preferred Qualifications
Candidate with additional skills in the following is preferred:
Experience implementing automated security testing (e.g., SonarQube, Fortify, Nexus/Artifactory scanning tools).
Exposure to radar, RF, or sensor systems and deploying software to hardware-in-the-loop (HWIL) environments.
Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools like Ansible, Terraform, or equivalent.
Familiarity with distributed applications or messaging frameworks (e.g., ZeroMQ).
Experience supporting web applications built with Angular TS, Flask, and SQL-based databases.
Knowledge of military cybersecurity standards or framework hardening (e.g., NIST SP 800-53, Risk Management Framework / RMF).

Rapidly build and deploy end-to-end AI systems and core components of generative AI solutions, owning the full arc from problem framing and MVP development to deployed workflow with a bias to action

Drive product advancements by developing robust RAG pipelines, context engineering workflows, and integrations with services like Azure AI Search and Databricks
Champion production discipline by implementing rigorous testing and evaluation frameworks, including golden sets, regression harnesses, and red-teaming to ensure secure, observable, and auditable code
Deliver in a fast-paced, outcome-accountable environment, operating in two-to-six-week cycles with direct client and stakeholder feedback to ensure solutions solve real-world problems and are ready for scale
Deploy and maintain scalable AI microservices and containerized workloads, optimizing performance and reliability to meet enterprise standards
Champion the use of modern development accelerators such as Claude Code, Lovable, Cursor, and others where policy permits, to increase delivery capacity and velocity while elevating code quality
Ensure software reliability and high code quality by writing unit tests, participating in code reviews, and utilizing CI/CD pipelines for automated builds and deployments
Engage in agile development processes including daily stand-ups, sprint planning, and retrospectives
Act with integrity, professionalism, and personal responsibility to uphold KPMG's respectful and courteous work environment
Qualifications:
Minimum three years of recent experience in software engineering with demonstrated success in building, testing, and shipping production AI, machine learning, or data-intensive applications
Master's degree from an accredited college or university in computer science, engineering, artificial intelligence, or a related technical field is preferred; minimum of a Bachelor's degree is required
Strong programming skills in Python; hands-on experience with modern AI/ML frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or Semantic Kernel
Practical knowledge of modern AI methodologies and engineering practices, including AI systems judgment, context engineering, agentic workflows, and evaluation discipline
Skilled within an agile environment using SDLC tools like Azure DevOps, Git, and CI/CD pipelines for automated builds and deployments
Solid experience with cloud platforms, preferably Azure (or GCP/AWS); familiar with containerization technologies like Docker and Kubernetes
Familiarity with modern AI-first developer accelerators (such as Cursor, Claude Code, or Copilot) to drive high-velocity development
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills; able to communicate technical ideas clearly, thrive in ambiguous environments, and collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders
Ability to demonstrate prior experience with real work via a portfolio, a GitHub repository, or a structured walk-through of a system designed and shipped
Domestic travel required
Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future; KPMG LLP will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work visa status for this opportunity (no sponsorship is available for H-1B, L-1, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, CPT or any other employment-based visa)

Amazon Web Services is a dynamic and rapidly growing business. We are building some of the largest and most complex distributed systems in the world and need world class people to help us implement and operate them.
You'll be part of a truly innovative team in a fast-paced environment that has the entrepreneurial feel of a start-up. This is an opportunity to operate and engineer systems on a massive scale, and to gain top-notch experience in cloud computing. You'll be surrounded by people who are passionate about cloud computing, and believe that world class service is critical to customer success. You'll become an expert at platform diagnosis, response, measurement, and automation. You will design and build the operational scalability that sustains the platform's insane growth.
A successful ADCE Engineer does much more than plug computers together and track changes. They are instrumental in deploying, operating, and scaling a massive always-on distributed system that is core to all of AWS. We are looking for a experienced and motivated engineer to join our fast-moving and passionate team.
This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance. The position further requires that, after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph or commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.
Basic Qualifications
High school or equivalent diploma, or A+ or CND (Certified Network Defender) or Network+ or Security+
1+ years of networking and troubleshooting experience
1+ years of systems administration (Linux/Windows) experience
Current, active US Government Security Clearance of Top Secret with SCI eligibility or above
Preferred Qualifications
High school or equivalent diploma, or certification in an applicable field like A+, Net+, Sec+, CCNA, LPIC, Linux+, AWS certification
3+ years of networking and troubleshooting experience
3+ years of systems administration (Linux/Windows) experience

Rare Candy is revolutionizing the $25 billion trading-card industry as the “friendly local game shop” in the palm of your hands. You won’t be handed endless tickets in a giant backlog. You’ll work on real product problems, learn from experienced engineers, and see your work directly improve the experience of passionate collectors.

You start the morning reviewing feedback on a feature you shipped yesterday and checking for backend errors.

Later in the day, you’re in a product discussion about how users want to showcase their favorite pulls, bringing both your backend perspective and your own TCG fluency to the conversation.

Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do.
Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.
Role Overview
Are you finishing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Electrical Engineering and looking to start your career where networking, AI infrastructure, and customer-facing technology meet? Keysight is hiring a Solution Engineer to join our Network and Application/Security (NAS) test team in Santa Clara.
As a Solution Engineer, you will learn to design and deliver technical solutions across Keysight's NAS test portfolio, working alongside experienced engineers who will mentor you through your first year. Our customers are the companies building the world's largest networks: hyperscale data center operators, cloud providers, and network equipment manufacturers. You will help them validate the networks that carry AI training workloads, cloud services, and global internet traffic.
This is a hands-on, customer-facing role. You will spend time in the lab building test topologies, and time with customers demonstrating how our solutions solve their validation challenges. We are looking for curiosity, strong fundamentals, and a genuine interest in networking. We will teach you the rest.
What You Will Do
Learn Keysight's NAS test portfolio and build hands-on expertise with our test platforms, including AI data center test solutions.
Build and maintain lab test topologies, running protocol and performance validation under the guidance of senior engineers.
Support product demonstrations and proof-of-concept efforts for customers, taking on more ownership as you ramp.
Participate in customer meetings and technical discussions, learning how to translate customer requirements into test solutions.
Write Python scripts to automate test execution, data collection, and reporting.
Help troubleshoot technical issues during customer evaluations, escalating to senior engineers as needed.
Develop demonstration materials and customer training content.
Learn the fundamentals of AI/ML back-end network fabrics, including RoCEv2/RDMA, lossless Ethernet (PFC, ECN, DCQCN), and GPU cluster validation.
Stay current on networking protocols, AI fabric technologies, and test automation practices.
Share customer feedback with our Engineering and Product Management teams.
Responsibilities
What We Are Looking For:
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, completed within the last 12 months or graduating by the start date.
Coursework or project experience in computer networks, covering TCP/IP fundamentals and Ethernet.
Working knowledge of Python, demonstrated through coursework, internships, or personal projects.
Comfort working hands-on with hardware in a lab environment.
Strong communication skills and genuine interest in a customer-facing technical role.
Curiosity, coachability, and a team-first approach.
Ability to travel up to 30% of work time.
Must be a U.S. Person as defined by U.S. export control regulations.
Qualifications
Desired:
Internship, co-op, research, or military experience in networking, systems, or test engineering.
Exposure to routing and data center protocols such as BGP, OSPF, VxLAN, or EVPN, in coursework or lab settings.
Network certification such as CCNA (or in progress).
Familiarity with Linux, Docker, Kubernetes, or public cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure).
Experience with packet analysis tools such as Wireshark.
Awareness of AI/ML data center networking concepts: RoCEv2/RDMA, congestion control, GPU cluster fabrics, or collective communication such as NCCL.
Experience with REST APIs or test automation frameworks.
Leadership in student organizations, hackathons, or technical competitions.
What You Will Gain
Structured onboarding and mentorship from senior Solution Engineers.
Hands-on experience with the industry's leading network test platforms, including AresONE 1600GE and Keysight AI Data Center Builder.
Direct exposure to the engineers building AI and cloud infrastructure at the world's largest technology companies.
A defined growth path from Associate to Advanced Solution Engineer.
Pay Range
USD $137,190.00 - USD $228,650.00 Year
Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.
Careers Privacy Statement***Keysight is an Equal Opportunity Employer.***

Description
Amazon Web Services is a dynamic and rapidly growing business. We are building some of the largest and most complex distributed systems in the world and need world class people to help us implement and operate them.
We provide organizations with building block web services that allow them to innovate faster and operate their software more cost-effectively. These services-in-the-cloud include on-demand compute capacity, storage, content delivery, querying of structured data, message queuing, and more.
The AWS Identity & Access team is building and delivering the next generation of cloud computing security that supports public AWS offerings like S3, EC2, and CloudFront. We are innovating new ways of building massively scalable distributed security systems involving identity management, federation, web services security, single sign-on, and much more. We enable our customers to control some of the most sensitive secrets on the Internet.
A successful ADCE Engineer does much more than plug computers together and track changes. They are instrumental in deploying, operating, and scaling a massive always-on distributed system that is core to all of AWS. We are looking for a experienced and motivated engineer to join our fast-moving and passionate team.
This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance. The position further requires that, after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph or commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.
About The Team
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Basic Qualifications
High school or equivalent diploma, or A+ or CND (Certified Network Defender) or Network+ or Security+
1+ years of networking and troubleshooting experience
1+ years of systems administration (Linux/Windows) experience
Current, active US Government Security Clearance of Top Secret or above
Preferred Qualifications
High school or equivalent diploma, or certification in an applicable field like A+, Net+, Sec+, CCNA, LPIC, Linux+, AWS certification
3+ years of systems administration (Linux/Windows) experience
3+ years of networking and troubleshooting experience
Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.
Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.
The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Company Description
Join a multibillion-dollar global company that brings together amazing technology, people, and operational scale to become a powerhouse in the memory industry. Headquartered in Rancho Cordova, California, Solidigm combines elements of an established, successful technology company with the spirit, agility, and entrepreneurial mindset of a start-up. In addition to the U.S. headquarters and other facilities in the U.S., the company has international presence in Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Solidigm will continue to lead the world in innovating new Memory technologies with aspirations to be the #1 NAND memory company in the world. At Solidigm, we view problems as opportunities to define innovative solutions that hold the power to change the world and unleash the potential technological needs that the future holds. At Solidigm, we are One Team that fosters a diverse, equitable, and inclusive culture that embraces individual uniqueness and empowers us to bring our best selves to deliver excellence in support of Solidigm's vision and mission to be the go-to partner for optimized data storage solutions. You can be part of the takeoff of an innovative business that develops cutting-edge products, delivers strong business value for customers, provides an engaging workplace for its employees, and serves a greater impact on the world. This is a golden opportunity for the right applicant to join us and help design, build, and lead Solidigm. We want a diverse team of dedicated professionals who will not just be Solidigm team members but contribute to how we shape the future of the organization. We are seeking applicants who will grow and thrive in our culture; be customer inspired, trusting, innovative, team-oriented, inclusive, results driven, collaborative, passionate, and flexible.
Job Description
This role is responsible for pre-silicon verification of advanced 3D NAND designs, including UVM-based verification, functional coverage, assertions, mixed-signal modeling and simulation, debugging, and verification-flow automation.
Key responsibilities
Create and maintain verification test plans based on design specifications.
Develop UVM-based directed and constrained-random tests, debug simulation failures, and quickly identify design, testbench, or test issues.
Define functional coverage models and perform coverage analysis and closure.
Create and maintain SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) for 3D NAND designs based on verification requirements.
Develop, maintain, and enhance the UVM-based verification environment to support evolving design and verification requirements.
Develop and maintain mixed-signal full-chip models and verification environments, including analog behavioral models, cell-level testbenches, and full-chip mixed-signal netlists and testbenches.
Develop scripts and tools to automate verification workflows, regression execution, results processing, and data collection.
Qualifications
Master’s degree with 3+ years of relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree with 5+ years, in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
Prior experience in pre-silicon verification of memory products is required.
Hands-on experience with UVM, SystemVerilog Assertions, and formal property verification.
Hands-on experience with mixed-signal verification, modeling, and simulation, supported by strong knowledge of digital and analog circuit design.
Strong data analysis capabilities, with the ability to communicate technical findings clearly through written reports and presentations.
Strong independent debugging and problem-solving skills, with proficiency in programming or scripting for design and verification automation.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across design, verification, modeling, and cross-functional teams.
Preferred qualifications include memory-industry verification experience, full-chip and regression verification, code and functional coverage closure, Python, Perl, or shell scripting, AI-assisted workflows, and commercial simulation, formal, and mixed-signal tools.
Additional Information
This position is also eligible to participate in Solidigm's restricted stock unit (RSU), restricted cash unit (RCU), and cash bonus programs. In addition, Solidigm offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, supplemental life and AD&D insurance; short- and long-term disability; healthcare and dependent care flexible spending accounts, and a company match on eligible 401(k) plan contributions.
The compensation range for this role is $121,280- $194,100. Actual compensation is influenced by a variety of factors including but not limited to skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location.
This is a Hybrid role reporting out of Rancho Cordova, California 3 days per week.

UF Information Technology (UFIT) is seeking a professional-level Research IT Engineer III to join Research Computing, a unit within UFIT.
UF Information Technology (UFIT) enables teaching, learning, research, and service on campus and across the region with state-of-the-art enterprise IT systems, including SEC and SUS universities, and the opportunity to teach using HiPerGator.

The demand for HiPerGator’s computing power to carry out research in foundational and use-inspired AI has also dramatically increased with UF’s AI Initiative and the recent success of generative AI such as ChatGPT in all aspects of human activity.

Job Description
:
This Warehouse Automation Engineering position can be responsible for he effort in identifying, evaluating, piloting and deploying new warehouse automation technologies, followed by the installation and deployment of new and optimizatoin of warehouse automation technologies. This dedicated teams and capability differentiates Ryder by driving efficiencies to grow existing and win new business. Support tracking of Punch List

Review team strategy with manager to set personal goals

Validate spend with manager

Partner with vendor to resolve Priority 1-5 tickets related to down/degregated performance with site automation
Join on P1/P1 Resolutions calls

Ability to work independently and as a member of a team., Required

Software Engineering
Job Details
About Salesforce
Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.
Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
Value Acceleration Engineer
AI agents can reason about what needs to happen. Getting them to reliably do work inside the software businesses actually run on is the next frontier.
We’re building Systems Integration Agent: computer use for the enterprise. It learns how to operate applications like SAP, Oracle, and Workday, then turns that knowledge into reusable, code-backed actions. The challenge goes beyond making an impressive demo: customers need automation they can trust with consequential business processes.
Our team operates as a small startup within Salesforce AI Labs, separate from the main engineering and product organizations. You’ll work directly with the team’s leader and engineers, alongside customers, with the autonomy to shape an early product and the resources of Salesforce to back you up.
As a Value Acceleration Engineer, you’ll write code, build alongside customers, and get real workflows into production. This is forward-deployed engineering on an emerging product: what you learn in deployments will help determine what we build next.
What You’ll Actually Be Doing
Build Directly With Customers
Work with process owners and customer IT to select workflows, define success, and secure the test access and data needed to build.
Run hands-on sessions that help customers use the product themselves, with clear scope and readiness expectations.
Help customers understand where the product can deliver value, explain its capabilities and limitations clearly, and connect technical results to business outcomes.
Engineer Reliable Automation
Write custom JavaScript tools when existing capabilities cannot complete a task.
Debug failures across browser behavior, agent execution, application state, and backend services.
Build tests for business outcomes, exceptions, partial completion, and recovery.
Help launch and stabilize workflows, documenting monitoring and recovery procedures and establishing support ownership with the team.
Make the Next Deployment Easier
Turn deployment lessons into reusable tools and tests, and work with core engineering to address recurring product gaps.
Use AI development tools thoughtfully while remaining accountable for code quality, security, and maintainability.
Working With Customers
Expect approximately 40–60% travel, typically several days onsite at a time, for customer discovery, hands-on build sessions, and launches.
You’re Our Person If…
You can write and debug JavaScript or TypeScript and reason about web applications, APIs, and data flow.
You enjoy working directly with users: asking precise questions, building alongside them, and explaining technical problems clearly.
You’ve independently shipped and operated production software, diagnosed failures, and improved the system afterward.
You can distinguish reliable behavior from something that happened to work once.
5+ years of relevant experience.
Helpful Experience
Playwright, browser automation, browser extensions, RPA, or enterprise integration.
Agent systems, tool execution, evaluations, or failure recovery.
SAP, Oracle, Workday, Salesforce, or similarly complex enterprise applications.
Forward-deployed engineering or customer-facing product development.
Unleash Your Potential
When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and
be your best
, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can
do your best
. Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.
